findings_fixed.fix_verified: _fileio.to_thread must be the same anyio.to_thread module. A proxy replacement is covered in the same fallback fixture.

reviewed_invariants: Only the verified official SDK 1.30.0 ordinary FastMCP/lowlevel/stdout construction path is optimized. Version, function origin, current method identity and bound receiver checks retain the original FastMCP.run path for supported custom/replaced cases.

The official stdio_server(stdout=adapter) remains the JSON-RPC serializer, newline framing loop and stdin reader. The same lowlevel server.run and create_initialization_options calls retain initialization, handlers, request context and lifespan ownership.

A successful output write executes native UTF-8 write(data) then native flush in one default run_sync worker, returning the original write count. Only a successful completion sets the one-use marker; no message text is retained across writes.

The immediately following single SDK writer flush consumes the marker and preserves an AnyIO cancellation/scheduling checkpoint. Independent/repeated flushes and post-error flushes execute the original native flush in a worker.

Write failures propagate without attempting flush. Flush failures propagate without a success marker. Default limiter and non-abandoning cancellation options remain unchanged; cancellation before dispatch prevents output, while already-started combined work completes before cancellation is observed at the next checkpoint.

Exact native TextIOWrapper/BufferedWriter-or-FileIO/FileIO output identities, native bound methods, open writable fd1, and the corresponding native input checks reject unsupported/custom streams before allocating an output wrapper.

The actual SDK test compares all five complete application response payloads, verifies ordinary result-cache writes/hit behavior, large Unicode output, five combined dispatches versus ten original write/flush dispatches, EOF completion and one MemoryBook.close per path.

No explicit standard-process handle close, protocol-loop replacement, response batching, alternate client, extra queue, retrieval bypass, result-cache suppression, dependency change or database schema change is introduced.
